name: Johnson 1892
description: An ornamental display face with rounded strokes, knob-ended curls, and an irregular rhythm.
observed: A–Z, a–z and 0–9 from the 1892 patent and period foundry specimens. Larger impressions inform title-critical forms.
reconstructed: Punctuation and symbols are newly drawn companions. Spacing is adapted for digital use.

sources.title: Herman Ihlenburg, US design patent D21,607 (1892), alphabet and figures
sources.rights: Historical US patent plate published 7 June 1892, beyond the maximum 95-year copyright term. The specification records a seven-year design-patent term. Evidence retained in reference/patent-rights.json.

sources.title: MacKellar, Smiths & Jordan, Specimens of Printing Types (1892), p. 274
sources.rights: Internet Archive records this 1892 edition as NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; metadata and copyright evidence retained in reference/msj-rights.json.

sources.title: H. Berthold specimen catalogue (1909), Zierschrift Skandia, p. 428
sources.rights: 1909 historical printing, treated as public domain in the supplied source record; publication predates the maximum US term

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (1894), printed p. 145; JP2 member 0151, corroborating the 60-point J
sources.rights: US publication from 1894, beyond the maximum 95-year term. Library of Congress metadata retained in reference/ryan-rights.json. Lossless PNG conversion of the historical JP2 page; used for comparison, not as a new tracing source.

revival.notes: Historical scans were deskewed, debris removed, and outlines fitted to the impressions. Original baseline irregularities and curled terminals are retained. In 1.002, H J L P R b f p q were retraced from recorded crops, removing stray scan marks and smoothing damaged stems. J uses the larger 60-point MSJ impression. Existing advances and kerning are preserved; see source/METHOD.md and the source/before-after proofs.
